# `integrations.microsoft_sentinel_auditlogs` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/integrations/microsoft-sentinel-auditlogs.satz`

## Purpose

The organisation's audit logs, on their way to Microsoft Sentinel.

NEEDS `presets/integrations/microsoft-sentinel.satz`: the connector authenticates
through the federation that file creates and reads as the account it creates.
Used without it, the compile stops with `unknown param 'sentinel_project_id'`.

FOUR RESOURCES, AND EACH ONE IS LOAD-BEARING: an organisation sink that exports
the four audit log streams with `include_children`, so every project is covered
and a project created tomorrow is covered too; the topic it writes to; the
subscription Sentinel pulls from; and two grants — `roles/pubsub.publisher` for
the sink's own writer identity, without which the sink exists and delivers
nothing, and `roles/pubsub.subscriber` for the Sentinel account on that one
subscription.

TIGHTER THAN UPSTREAM ON PURPOSE. Microsoft's published configuration grants a
project-level custom role carrying `pubsub.subscriptions.consume` and `.get`,
which reaches every subscription in the project, including ones this estate did
not make. The predefined `roles/pubsub.subscriber` on this subscription alone is
the same access where it is needed and none where it is not.

THE FILTER IS OR-ONLY. Cloud Logging charges a sink nothing for what it exports,
but an `AND`, a `NOT` or a `!=` in an organisation sink's filter narrows it per
project in ways that are hard to read back; the audit streams are named as four
alternatives, exactly as the archive sink names them. Data access logs are in the
list and are the loud half of the volume — Sentinel's own ingestion is charged by
the gigabyte, so an estate that does not want them drops that one `log_id`.

ONE SOURCE, NOT ALL OF THEM. Microsoft publishes a configuration per log source —
VPC flow, firewall, DNS, GKE, Cloud SQL, Compute, IAM, Resource Manager and the
rest — each its own topic, subscription and sink. This is the audit-log one,
which every customer starts with. Another source is this file with its own
names and filter; copy it rather than widening this sink, because a sink is
replaced when its filter changes and the replacement drops what was in flight.

NO CLAIM. Exporting audit logs to a SIEM does not satisfy a retention control:
`monitoring/organization-audit-logsink.satz` is what claims those, and this sink
is a copy leaving the organisation, not the archive.

## Use it

```
params {
  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  sentinel_auditlogs_topic = "sentinel-topic"
  sentinel_auditlogs_subscription = "sentinel-subscription-auditlogs"
  sentinel_auditlogs_sink_name = "audit-logs-organization-sentinel-sink"
  sentinel_auditlogs_filter = "log_id("cloudaudit.googleapis.com/activity") OR log_id("cloudaudit.googleapis.com/data_access") OR log_id("cloudaudit.googleapis.com/system_event") OR log_id("cloudaudit.googleapis.com/policy")"
  sentinel_auditlogs_retention = "604800s"
  sentinel_auditlogs_ack_deadline_seconds = 60
}

use "presets/integrations/microsoft-sentinel-auditlogs.satz"
```

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_organization_id` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `sentinel_project_id` — declared by `integrations.microsoft_sentinel`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sentinel_auditlogs_filter` | Which audit logs travel to Sentinel — all four streams, or without data access? | recreate | low | — |

**sentinel_auditlogs_filter** — Data Access logs are most of the volume, and Sentinel is charged by the gigabyte ingested: leaving them in buys full visibility of who read what, taking them out cuts the bill and the answer to that question with it. The organisation's own archive keeps whatever this sink drops. Widening it later replaces the sink, and what was in flight at that moment is not re-sent.
